title: AI companies back a shared robots.txt training opt-out
summary: Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic support a common website signal intended to simplify how publishers reject AI training use.
body:
## What happened
Major AI companies are backing a shared policy token for robots.txt that would let websites express AI-training preferences once instead of maintaining separate instructions for each crawler. Google said it plans to interpret the proposed token as a disallow for Google-Extended when no more specific Google-Extended rule is present.

The proposal comes from work in the IETF’s AIPREF process. Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic have publicly indicated support, while Meta has also been reported as engaging with the effort. The signal is designed to cover participating providers rather than create another company-specific crawler rule.

## Why it matters
The move addresses a practical problem for publishers: today’s opt-out controls differ by provider and may distinguish training, search grounding, and product access. A shared token could lower the technical burden for smaller websites and make publisher preferences easier for crawlers to interpret consistently.

The announcement is not a licensing settlement and does not force every AI company or crawler to comply. It also leaves important questions open, including how providers will document enforcement, how conflicts between broad and provider-specific rules will be resolved, and whether opting out of training will affect search or answer-generation products separately.

For the AI industry, the significance is institutional rather than immediate. If the signal becomes widely implemented, it could become basic web infrastructure for negotiating access to public content. If adoption remains voluntary and uneven, publishers may still need a patchwork of vendor-specific controls.

## Uncle Cat take
The useful deliverable is the shared token, but its value depends on crawler compliance records that have not yet been promised.
title_zh: 主要AI公司支持统一的robots.txt训练退出信号
summary_zh: 谷歌、微软、OpenAI和Anthropic支持一种通用网站信号，拟简化出版商拒绝AI训练使用内容的方式。
body_zh:
## 发生了什么
多家主要AI公司支持在robots.txt中加入统一策略标记，让网站只需一次声明，就能表达对AI训练的偏好，而不必为每个爬虫维护不同规则。谷歌表示，如果网站使用这一标记且没有单独指定Google-Extended规则，它计划将其解释为禁止Google-Extended。

该方案来自IETF的AIPREF工作。谷歌、微软、OpenAI和Anthropic已公开表示支持，Meta也被报道参与了相关讨论。这个信号面向参与的多家服务商，目标是减少企业自定义爬虫规则的数量。

## 为什么重要
它解决的是出版商面对的实际管理难题：不同公司的退出机制并不一致，有些还会区分模型训练、搜索抓取和产品接入。统一标记有望降低小型网站的技术负担，也让爬虫更容易一致理解网站意愿。

但这不是版权许可协议，也不会强迫所有AI公司或爬虫执行。训练退出是否会影响搜索或答案生成、通用规则与单家公司规则冲突时如何处理，以及各方如何公开执行记录，仍没有答案。

对AI行业而言，这更像制度基础设施的起点，而不是即时商业结果。如果主要爬虫广泛落实，它可能成为互联网内容授权的新底层规则；如果执行仍然自愿且不完整，网站依旧要维护供应商专属设置。

## Uncle Cat判断
统一标记本身只是半成品，真正的价值要等各家公开爬虫合规记录后才能兑现。
